newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK foreign reserves up 15 pct at US$63.8 bln in 96.
newsitem.headline: HK foreign reserves up 15 pct at US$63.8 bln in 96.

text.p: Hong Kong's foreign reserves were up 15 percent year-on-year at US$63.8 billion at the end of December 1996, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said in a statement on Friday.
On this basis, Hong Kong has maintained its ranking of holding the world's seventh largest foreign reserves, the authority said.
Including forward transactions to be settled, Hong Kong's foreign reserves at the end of 1996 were US$69.6 billion, up 22 percent from US$57.2 billion recorded at the end of 1995.
All these reserves do not include foreign reserves held in the Land Fund, said the HKMA, the territory's de facto central bank.
The HKMA also said figures on foreign reserves held in the Exchange Fund will be released on a monthly basis instead of the previous quarterly basis.
